releases.body:
# v0.49.80

This patch fixes six defects reported from a code review of 0.49.78, three in the OpenCode 2 adapter and three in background maintenance and memory search. It also fixes two more OpenCode 2 defects found while reviewing those fixes.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: a `/btw` side question after an interrupted turn could be sent unmanaged history** (issue 981). When a turn was refused before Magic Context had processed it, the unprocessed request replaced the one saved for side questions. A side question asked next could then go out with the raw session history. A request is now saved only after it has been processed, and a refused turn of any kind leaves the saved one as it was.
- **OpenCode 2: text removed by a revert could come back in a later request** (issue 979). After a revert, a new host checkpoint could reuse the number of a checkpoint from before the revert and be served that older checkpoint's summary, which still described the reverted text. A stored summary now belongs to one checkpoint only. A session that already carries such a mixed record, including one that already sent the old summary, rebuilds its history once after the upgrade. That costs the session one prompt-cache rewrite.
- **OpenCode 2: a failed model list request no longer stops every turn** (issue 980). When the host could not list its models, every turn on a model not seen before was interrupted with `usage-unavailable`, although the model's limits were known from the request. Magic Context now uses those limits until the model list works again. A request that is too large for the model is still refused.
- **OpenCode 2: an OpenCode process left running on an older Magic Context could send unmanaged history.** When another process upgraded the Magic Context database while an OpenCode 2 process with an older plugin kept running, that older process sent its requests without context management and without any warning. It now refuses the turn and tells you to restart OpenCode, as OpenCode 1 already does. As documented for `fail_closed_blocking`, the refusal applies to your own prompts, not to OpenCode's title and summary requests, and setting `fail_closed_blocking: false` turns it off; OpenCode 2 now follows that setting when the database cannot be opened at startup too.
- **OpenCode 2: part of a message could be missing after a compaction.** If a summary ended in the middle of a message, the rest of that message was left out of requests after the next host compaction. Nothing was deleted from the store. This could only happen with summaries written by the experimental Rust mode, on a message that gained a tool result after it was summarized. An affected session gets the missing part back on its first request after the upgrade.
- **Docs upkeep skipped commits made while a proposal was waiting** (issue 982). A `maintain-docs` run that found a proposal still pending recorded the newest commit as reviewed. Commits made in the meantime were never looked at, whether the proposal was then applied or dismissed. A waiting run no longer moves that marker.
- **Memory search could compare vectors from two embedding models** (issue 983). If the embedding model was changed while a search was running, memories embedded with the new model could be scored against a query embedded with the old one. Search now only uses vectors from the query's own model.
- **A memory edited during summarization could keep the embedding of its old text** (issue 984). When several new memories were embedded one after another and one was edited while it waited, it was embedded from its old text and never corrected, so search by meaning kept matching the old wording. The text is now read at the moment it is embedded. Embeddings stored this way before the fix are not rewritten.

Issues 982, 983 and 984 also affected Pi and Oh My Pi.

# v0.49.79

This patch fixes the weekly memory tidy-up reporting a failure when it had nothing safe to change, and keeps a safety net for OpenCode 2 sessions that hold an image.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **A tidy-up run whose every proposed change was refused is no longer a failure** (issue 978). The `curate` task lets a model propose updates and archives, and safety checks refuse a change that would lose content or archive a memory with no live successor. When every proposal was refused, the run ended as `MC-D06 · Curate returned no completed ctx_memory tool result`, was counted as a model failure, and was retried on the fallback model for the same result. Such a run now completes and says what happened, for example `curate: no changes; 4 operations refused (content-loss ×2, missing-active-same-category-successor ×2)`. No fallback model is tried. A run that applied some changes and had others refused reports both. A run that only read memories and decided to change nothing also completes.
- **The tidy-up no longer stays on one category.** The task works through one memory category per run. It moved to the next category only after a completed run, so a category that failed the same way every time kept its turn and the others never ran. It now also moves on after a failure that a retry cannot fix. A provider error or timeout still retries the same category.
- **Pi and Oh My Pi: a refused tidy-up change was reported as applied.** The run detail said `1 memory operation applied` when the safety checks had refused the change and no memory was touched. Pi now reports refusals the way OpenCode does.
- **OpenCode 2: a session with an image keeps its fallback when the store is briefly busy.** When Magic Context's store is locked for a moment, the plugin resends the last good request instead of refusing the turn. A saved request that held an image could never be resent, because its size could not be measured, so such a session had its turn refused. The saved image is now measured like the live one, and the resent request is byte-identical to the original.

# v0.49.78

This patch fixes OpenCode 2 sessions that fail on every prompt after an image attachment is restored.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart OpenCode. No database migration is needed. A session that was already failing works again on its next prompt, with no manual repair. Pi, Oh My Pi and OpenCode 1 users are not affected and can update whenever they like.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: a restored image could make every turn of a session fail** (issue 977). After a host compaction, Magic Context rebuilds older messages from the store. An image attachment in such a message could be handed to OpenCode in an outdated shape, and OpenCode 2.3 then failed the request before it reached any model, on every later prompt, with `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'e.source.data.length')`. It happened when the first draft a freshly started plugin saw began with a system message, which OpenCode 2.3 writes for a reasoning-effort or model change: the plugin then decided, for as long as OpenCode kept running, that the host did not need the newer attachment shape. The decision no longer depends on which message comes first, and the outdated shape is removed, since no supported OpenCode 2 version accepts it.
- **OpenCode 2: an attachment the host cannot use no longer stops the request.** The last step before a request is handed back to OpenCode now checks every image part. One the host could not use is rebuilt in the form the host needs, so the image still reaches the model. When that is not possible, and when a restored attachment cannot be rebuilt at all, a short text note takes its place, so the rest of the message still reaches the model.

# v0.49.77

This patch makes Magic Context load again on Oh My Pi 19.2.0.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed. OpenCode and Pi users are not affected and can update whenever they like.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi 19.2.0 refused to load the Magic Context extension.** Oh My Pi 19.2.0 no longer accepts an extension that imports Pi's terminal UI package, so Magic Context did not start: sessions ran without context management. The extension now uses the terminal UI of the host it runs in. On Oh My Pi 19.1 and earlier, and on Pi, nothing changes.
- **Oh My Pi 19.2.0 refused Magic Context's background runs.** Summary and maintenance runs start a hidden Oh My Pi child with no tools. Oh My Pi 19.2.0 rejects the flag Magic Context used for that when an extension is loaded at startup. Hidden runs on Oh My Pi now ask for an empty tool list instead. The check that such a run really has no tools is unchanged.
- **The status screen and the todo list work on Oh My Pi 19.2.0.** Oh My Pi 19.2.0 also changed how extensions draw custom screens. `/ctx-status`, the todo list above the prompt and the todo tool's display now draw the new way on 19.2.0 and the old way on earlier versions and on Pi. If a host offers neither, Magic Context still loads and `/ctx-status` shows its summary as a plain notice.

releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.21.1
releases.body:
## Fixes

- **Linux AppImage: model checks no longer create stray projects.** The dashboard asks OpenCode which models are available. On a Linux AppImage, those checks ran inside the AppImage's temporary mount folder, so OpenCode saw that folder as a new project each time. They now run from Magic Context's data folder, or your home folder when the data folder setting is blank or relative. Thanks to the reporter of issue #964 for the fix.
